ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle ABD = \angle CBE = 90^\circ$, $AB = BD$, $\angle CAB = \angle E$. If $BE = 10$, $AD = 4\sqrt{2}$ , what is the value of $\frac{AC}{DE}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
Since $\angle ABD=90^\circ$ and $AB=BD$, $AD=4\sqrt{2}$, \\
therefore $2AB^{2}=2BD^{2}=AD^{2}$, \\
hence $2AB^{2}=32$, solving this yields: $AB=BD=4$ (taking the positive value); \\
Since $\angle ABD=\angle CBE=90^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle ABD-\angle CBD=\angle CBE-\angle CBD$, \\
therefore $\angle ABC=\angle DBE$, \\
and since $\angle CAB=\angle E$, \\
it can be concluded that $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle EBD$, \\
therefore $\frac{AC}{DE}=\frac{AB}{BE}=\frac{4}{10}=\boxed{\frac{2}{5}}$.
